newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation still high in Lehman.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation still high in Lehman.

text.p: Takeover speculation in Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc remained high Thursday, keeping volatilities firm, even though the shares gave back most of Wednesday's gains.
The stock rallied 6-3/4 points on Wednesday, most of it in the afternoon, amid fresh takeover talk.
Lehman was rumored to be the buyout target of Chase Manhattan Corp. Chase and Lehman declined comment.
By late Thursday, Lehman shares were off 4-7/16 at 47-9/16, but speculation the broker would be bought out remained solid, traders said.
"There's still speculation out there," said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners in New York.
"Volatility, which had spiked yesterday, maintained higher levels for both puts and calls," he said, explaining that institutional and retail demand was mostly for calls on Wednesday.
Todd Raarup, a market maker in Lehman options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, said volatility in the September out-of-the-money options was around 55, down roughly 10 points from Wednesday.
"Volatility came down a little bit just because it didn't get taken over," he said. "Last night it looked pretty serious."
He added that before the takeover talk, volatility in the options was around the 40 level.
Traders said Thursday's activity in Lehman options was much slower than on Wednesday, and Schwarz added that most of the action was from retail customers.
"The institutions seem to be sitting on the side," he said.
Raarup noted that Lehman often spikes on takeover rumors only to ease back down when the rumored deal fails to materialize.
In May, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc was rumored to be eyeing Lehman, leading to a similar spike-and-retreat in Lehman's shares.
"Once an expiration cycle you get a spike but yesterday was probably the most active I've ever seen in that stock," Raarup said, referring to Lehman.
Activity Thursday was led by the August 50 calls, which traded a total of about 2,750 contracts.
Other actives included the August 45 calls and the September 55 calls. Among the puts, the August 45s traded nearly 1,000 contracts.
"There's good demand and also some sellers here of both," Schwarz said.
Lehman options trade on the American Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
